x: Damage limitation was achieved as William Sharman cleared 4 metres for a season’s best and junior Roy Collier equalled his best to get better than expected B points.

William Sharman claimed top spot on his own this year as only he, Mick Jones and new member Adrian Phillips made all four matches. There will be some serious revisions to the all time points scores table as many of our big points scorers continued to rack up impressive contributions to the team’s efforts.

The ever reliable Will Cockerell produced one point more than anticipated in the steeplechase and then came our only maximum point event of the day as William Sharman won the A 110H in deteriorating conditions and Dom Girdler did likewise in the B race.
Non specialists William Sharman and James Everard performed well in the high jump but the competition was so classy that they made little impression on the points.

William Sharman has been named the first UK Challenge Athlete of the Month winner, for his performances during May. The Belgrave Harrier scored a total of 375 points, thanks to a 13.85w 110 hurdles victory in the Inter Counties Championships at Bedford and a 14.22 win in the first round of the Briti…

Back on the track, William Sharman again eased to victory in the A 110 hurdles clocking a fine 13.85 secs into a big headwind. A tired Dom Girdler dragged himself over the barriers to win the B and complete yet another max points performance for our sprint hurdlers.
With William Sharman in Gothenberg, Dom Girdler seamlessly stepped into the A 110 hurdles and despite lack of training due to heavy work commitments finished a good second in the A race.
Drawn in the first heat of the sprint hurdles William Sharman was up against the outstanding Frenchman Ladji Doucouré but it was the Swede Kronborg who made the running.

William Sharman was doubtful to race following a lengthy lay off due to injury but did support the team to gain silver in the high hurdles. Darren Chin gained good points in the hotly contested sprints.
More good points came in the sprint hurdles where William Sharman ran a season’s best for second followed by an unexpected victory by Kevin Sempers in the B.
Our two wins were on the track with William Sharman getting the photo decision following an apparent dead heat with Moscow’s Borisov. Later William led off our victorious sprint relay squad.
With top point scorers William Sharman and Darren Chin on their way to the World Student Games and Joe Ive injured, we cast the net wide to chase every point.

Also competing on day one was William Sharman who cruised through his heat securing third spot for a place in the semi’s. Unfortunately he false started and then dwelt in the blocks (0.235 sec reaction time) trailing in last in his slowest time of the year.

And just before this William Sharman posted a huge season’s best to win the A high hurdles in 13.70 sec. Even more bouncy than usual he was rewarded with last leg in the long relay and to the surprise of everyone he held form to the line but was completely shattered in the process.

Mark Allen, who had spent three months earlier in the year joining William Sharman under the command of John Anderson filming Gladiators for Sky TV, had promised us good results from a truncated training regime.
William Sharman placed 3rd in the sprint hurdles final, Tim Bayley was 5th in the 800m and Hannah Douglas was 7th in the 400m hurdles, not too far from her best time.

William Sharman completed his fourth win of the season in the sprint hurdles and gained third spot in the B 200. The 800m provided fast races but we achieved good points with Steve Davies finishing fourth in the A race and Neil Speaight second in the B event.
Michaela Hutchison won the women’s B 800m final but there was disappointment for William Sharman as he accompanied Andy Turner out of the 60 metres hurdles final after they both false started.
